title: Electron configuration
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: How do I know which order to fill the electrons?
Is it always two, eight, eight for the first three periods?
What is the difference between s and p orbitals?

explain.say: Today we are learning about electron configuration. This shows where electrons are found around an atom.
Electrons fill energy levels, or shells, in a specific order. The first shell holds a maximum of two electrons.
The second shell can hold up to eight electrons, which is the most common pattern we see. For example, neon has ten electrons.
The third shell can hold up to eighteen electrons, but we often use the two, eight, eight rule for simplicity. Consider the element magnesium.
We also use s, p, and d notation for specific orbitals. The s orbital holds two electrons, while the p orbital holds up to six electrons.
For a real-life example, think about the structure of a water molecule. Oxygen has 8 electrons, filling its shells according to these rules.

faq.q: Why do I always start with two electrons in the first shell?
faq.a: The first shell, or the n equals one level, can only accommodate a maximum of two electrons. This is a fundamental rule of atomic structure.
asks: What is the limit of the first shell?
Can the first shell hold more than two electrons?

faq.q: When do I switch from the two, eight, eight rule to the full capacity?
faq.a: You use the two, eight, eight rule for the first few elements. For larger atoms, you must follow the actual maximum capacity of the shells.
asks: What is the correct capacity for the third shell?

faq.q: What does the 's' notation tell me about the electrons?
faq.a: The 's' notation refers to the spherical s orbital, which can hold a maximum of two electrons. It is the first type of orbital filled.
asks: What does s stand for in electron configuration?
How many electrons fit in an s orbital?

faq.q: Is the order of filling always s then p then d?
faq.a: Yes, for the same energy level, electrons fill into the s orbital first, then the p orbitals, and finally the d orbitals.
asks: What is the filling order for orbitals?
Do I fill s or p first?

faq.q: How many electrons are in the second shell of chlorine?
faq.a: Chlorine has 17 electrons total. It will have eight electrons in its second shell, following the two, eight, eight pattern.
asks: What is the second shell count for Cl?

facts: The first electron shell has a maximum capacity of two electrons.
The second electron shell can hold up to eight electrons.
Orbitals are designated by letters: s, p, and d.
The electron configuration shows the distribution of electrons across energy levels.

quiz.say: An atom with 10 electrons has electrons filling shells of:
quiz.why: The first shell holds a maximum of two, and the second shell holds the remaining eight electrons.

wrong.0: This incorrectly assumes three shells are needed for only ten electrons.
wrong.1: This lists the total number of electrons, not how they are distributed across shells.
wrong.2: This incorrectly suggests the maximum capacity of the second shell is six.

quiz.say: Which orbital type can hold a maximum of six electrons?
quiz.why: The p orbital type is known to accommodate a maximum of six electrons.

wrong.0: While d orbitals hold more, the question asks for the one that holds six.
wrong.1: Shell 2 is a level, not a specific orbital type.
wrong.3: The s orbital is limited to only two electrons.

quiz.say: If an atom has 12 electrons, the configuration using shells is:
quiz.why: Following the two, eight, eight rule, the first two shells fill to ten, leaving two for the third shell.

wrong.1: This incorrectly suggests the second shell can hold ten electrons.
wrong.2: This only accounts for ten electrons, leaving two unplaced.
wrong.3: This does not follow the established rules for filling the second and third shells.
